title: Heuristic laddering usability sprint notes — Nov 2026
body:
Context and goal:
- 3-day lab sprint to surface highest-impact console friction for model rollout and routing flows.
- Technique: heuristic laddering (start broad heuristics, drill to specific microtasks + participant rationale).
- Participants: 6 product engineers (mid-stage startups), 4 ML infra/platform engineers (enterprise), 2 solutions engineers — total 12. Remote moderated sessions (60m) + 15m follow-up card-sort.

Method quick notes:
- Warm-up: 5m prompts about last week using Redwood console (open answer).
- Task scenarios: 5 canonical tasks mapped to onboarding->deploy->observe->rollback. Each task timed (goal 5-10m).
- Laddering: after task, ask "why" twice to get to motivation and expectation (e.g., why do you care about latency breakdown?).
- Scoring: Nielsen-style heuristics rated 1–5 for each task; we capture exemplar quotes and screenshots of the wireframe iterations used.

High-level findings (synthesized):
1) Discoverability vs. noise: users want quick access to routing/fallback config but are overwhelmed by too many toggles on the primary model settings screen. Common quote: "I want one place to say 'if this model degrades, use X' not five scattered toggles."
2) Latency breakdown mental model mismatch: engineers expect end-to-end trace (client->router->model) but console shows per-model stage only. Leads to false confidence.
3) Rollout affordance is unclear: canaries and A/B need clearer success criteria input (what constitutes success). Participants attempted to enter SLOs but hit validation errors.
4) Bulk operations anxiety: bulk model pinning and route reassignment lack dry-run preview. Users worried about accidental mass changes.
5) Observability onboarding gap: first-time users didn't know how to attach prompts/evals to an existing route; they expected a single CTA.

Wireframe-specific notes (iteration references included):
- Wireframe A (single page model settings): good at grouping, but too many inline dropdowns. Suggested: collapse advanced toggles behind a "performance" accordion.
- Wireframe B (routing matrix view): participants liked matrix metaphor but wanted direct edit cells (inline edit) and an undo/preview action.
- New micro-interaction suggestion: hover preview of fallback chain showing estimated latency delta and cost delta.

Heuristic laddering scores (median across participants, scale 1=poor,5=good):
- Visibility of system status: 3
- Match between system and real-world: 2
- User control and freedom (rollback/undo): 2
- Error prevention: 2
- Recognition vs recall (labels/affordances): 3
- Flexibility and efficiency of use: 4

Representative participant quotes (verbatim where possible):
- "I shouldn't need to guess which fallback is in place after a failure."
- "Show me the cost impact before I flip the toggle."
- "If a model degrades in accuracy I want automatic rerouting, but only if latency isn't impacted."

Metrics observed (lab):
- Task completion: onboarding->deploy flow 75% success (expected 90% for mature product).
- Median time on routing task: 8m 40s. Friction points: validation errors and unclear state.
- Card-sort consistency: 82% of enterprise participants grouped routing and SLA controls together.

Backlog grooming (proposed tickets with priority and acceptance criteria):
- CON-1543: Add "Routing preview" modal (priority: P0). Acceptance: preview shows fallback chain, estimated cost delta, estimated latency delta; user can confirm/dry-run.
- CON-1547: Consolidate fallback toggles into single "Fallback policy" panel with presets and advanced editor (priority: P1). Acceptance: UI has presets (safe, aggressive) + JSON editor; unit tests for preset selection.
- CON-1551: Add SLO field with inline validation and example presets to rollout wizard (priority: P0). Acceptance: user can set SLO, invalid inputs rejected with actionable message; wizard blocks rollout without success criteria.
- CON-1560: Bulk-change dry-run checkbox + audit preview (priority: P1). Acceptance: when bulk action chosen, dry-run modal shows list of affected routes and diff.

Quick wins (can ship in 1 sprint):
- Add hover tooltip on model settings for current active fallback (low dev cost).
- Improve error messaging on SLO validation with examples (copy update only).

Design notes / wireframe tasks for next sprint:
- Sketch inline cell editing for routing matrix and a compact undo/preview microflow.
- Mock hover preview with synthetic cost/latency numbers and microcopy explaining how estimates computed.
- Run 5 remote guerilla tests with customers after implementing hover preview and SLO message (metrics: task completion, perceived confidence).

Open questions / research backlog:
- Does the hover preview reduce cognitive load or just add a new learning surface? (A/B test).
- What's the best default for fallback presets for SMB vs. Enterprise? (data + interview).
- Should we support policy templates tied to Dedicated vs Hosted modes? (impact on RBAC & config).

Action items (owners + due):
- Priya: prototype routing matrix inline edit (lo-fi) by 2026-11-17.
- Alex: PR for SLO inline validation copy and unit tests by 2026-11-12.
- Riley: draft CON-1543 ticket with UX acceptance criteria and mockups by 2026-11-15.
- Noah: run follow-up microtests (5 sessions) after prototype ready; capture metric baseline.

Notes to self:
- Preserve verbatim quotes in final synthesis doc for customer empathy.
- Link recordings to CON tickets; redact customer-identifying info.
- Consider including a short video clip in the roadmap deck to show pain point in action.

Appendix: session artifacts and misc observations:
- Participant 3 (enterprise infra): always asked "what happens on failover" before touching any config — strong sign the default state must be visible.
- Participant 9 (startup SE): kept opening the wrong modal because the iconography reused gear icon for different contexts — replace with clearer icons.
- Slack thread referencing this sprint: #ux-routing-sprint (see pinned messages).

End of notes.
